'''''Crassula natans''''', commonly known as '''floating pigmyweed''',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/119460-Crassula-natans|title=Floating Pigmyweed Crassula natans|accessdate=12 September 2017|work=iNaturalist|publisher=California Academy of Sciences}}</ref> is a herb in the family [[Crassulaceae]].<ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|name=''Crassula natans''|id=3142}}</ref>

This [[Annual plant|annual]] herb is often found in an aquatic environment. It blooms between July and November producing white-pink flowers.<ref name=FloraBase/> The plant has decumbent filiform branches that are around {{convert|10|cm|in|1}} in length and are often multi-branched when growing in marshy area, or slender floating branches up to {{convert|25|cm|in|1|abbr=on}} in length. It has linear shaped leaves linear approximately {{convert|8|mm|in|2}} long and {{convert|1|mm|in|3|abbr=on}} wide in marsh plants, or for floating plants with a length of {{convert|14|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} and a width of {{convert|2|mm|in|3|abbr=on}}.<ref name=sas/>

The plant is [[endemism|endemic]] to the wetlands of Cape Fold area of the Western Cape region of [[South Africa]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The Status and Distribution of Freshwater Biodiversity in Southern Africa|author=Will Darwall|author2=D. Tweddle|author3=K. Smith|author4=P. Skelton|name-list-style=amp|publisher=IUCN|year=2009|isbn=9782831711263}}</ref>
It has become naturalised in Western Australia where it is found in winter wet depressions and in gullies and lakes in the [[Great Southern (Western Australia)|Great Southern]], [[Wheatbelt (Western Australia)|Wheatbelt]], [[South West (Western Australia)|South West]] and [[Peel (Western Australia)|Peel]] regions.<ref name=FloraBase/> It is also found throughout southern [[South Australia]], [[New South Wales]] and [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]].<ref name=sas>{{cite web|url=http://saseedbank.com.au/species_information.php?rid=1248|title=Crassula natans var. minus (Crassulaceae) Floating Crassula|accessdate=12 September 2017|work=Seeds of South Australia|publisher=[[Government of South Australia]]}}</ref>

== Botany ==
The plants often grow in and around shallow standing water of rock pools and dams. On moist soil, the plants are often a deep red, tufted and below 2.4 inches, and with 3 flowers per node. When submerged, the buoyant branches can reach up to 14 inches (35 cm) in length and are enlarged at the base, where they support narrow linear leaves, whereas the floating leaves are oblong and much broader, and only occasionally produce more than one flower per node.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=WoS |date=2018-04-13 |title=Crassula natans (Floating Pigmyweed) |url=https://worldofsucculents.com/crassula-natans-floating-pigmyweed/ |access-date=2025-09-03 |website=World of Succulents |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Flower ===
The flowers are often white and cup-shaped, they can be white or pink<ref name="auto"/>
